title: The Boy on the Stairs  (Le garçon sur l'escalier)

segments.t: En sortant dans la cour baignée de soleil, Mademoiselle Evelyn raconte à Hannah l'histoire des deux frères du numéro douze, sans voir que Caleb vient de descendre l'escalier extérieur juste derrière elles. Tendez d'abord l'oreille.
Tell me more about the two boys on Linden Street, Miss Evelyn!
The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.
And the younger brother with the wooden train?
Quiet as a mouse! He sat on the third stair listening to every single note.
Listening to the sound of the room... wait a second!
Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer when it rained.
Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the stone street...
Caleb! Were you standing right there?!
Good heavens... look at your eyes! Little Caleb from the third stair?!
Miss Evelyn?! My brother's Friday piano teacher?!
Wait, then Monday night on our step... the second blue suitcase...
Yes, Hannah. That blue suitcase is mine, and I owe you both the whole truth.
Reprenons phrase après phrase ce grand moment d'émotion dans la cour.
Tell me more about the two boys on Linden Street, Miss Evelyn!
'Racontez-m'en davantage sur les deux garçons de la rue du Tilleul, Mademoiselle Evelyn!'
The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.
'Le frère aîné était hardi et bruyant, il expédiait toujours ses gammes à toute allure.'
And the younger brother with the wooden train?
'Et le petit frère au train en bois?'
Quiet as a mouse! He sat on the third stair listening to every single note.
'Sage comme une image! Il s'asseyait sur la troisième marche en écoutant chacune des notes.'
Listening to the sound of the room... wait a second!
'En écoutant la résonance de la pièce... attendez une seconde!'
Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer when it rained.
'Chaque fois que je finissais de jouer, il demandait pourquoi le piano sonnait plus rond quand il pleuvait.'
Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the stone street...
'Parce que des volets en bois mouillés adoucissent l'écho de la rue pavée...'
Caleb! Were you standing right there?!
'Caleb! Vous étiez juste là?!'
Good heavens... look at your eyes! Little Caleb from the third stair?!
'Bonté divine... regarde tes yeux! Le petit Caleb de la troisième marche?!'
Miss Evelyn?! My brother's Friday piano teacher?!
'Mademoiselle Evelyn?! La professeure de piano du vendredi de mon frère?!'
Wait, then Monday night on our step... the second blue suitcase...
'Attendez, alors lundi soir sur notre marche... la deuxième valise bleue...'
Yes, Hannah. That blue suitcase is mine, and I owe you both the whole truth.
'Oui, Hannah. Cette valise bleue est à moi, et je vous dois à toutes les deux toute la vérité.'
Réécoutons une dernière fois toute la scène d'un seul souffle.
Tell me more about the two boys on Linden Street, Miss Evelyn!
The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.
And the younger brother with the wooden train?
Quiet as a mouse! He sat on the third stair listening to every single note.
Listening to the sound of the room... wait a second!
Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer when it rained.
Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the stone street...
Caleb! Were you standing right there?!
Good heavens... look at your eyes! Little Caleb from the third stair?!
Miss Evelyn?! My brother's Friday piano teacher?!
Wait, then Monday night on our step... the second blue suitcase...
Yes, Hannah. That blue suitcase is mine, and I owe you both the whole truth.

Quel coup de théâtre sous le tilleul! Le petit garçon de la troisième marche se tient juste devant sa professeure de piano d'autrefois, et la valise mystère lui appartient! Rendez-vous au cinquième épisode! À très bientôt!
Goodbye!
